blocos.texto: Aatrox wants to poke or combo you with his Qs. Make sure to dodge as many as possible. Deny the sweet spots at all costs. His Qs don't deal a lot of damage while he is level 1-3, but starting level 4, the damage ramps up significantly. Aatrox struggles against champions that can stay on top of him.
Don't let Aatrox crash waves continuously, or he can use his Qs to poke you under tower while using the knock-up to deny your last hits.
Level 1: Take E if Aatrox threatens you with Qs from the beginning. If he plays passive, start with Q.

Being able to poke or trade mostly depends on Aatrox's E and Q casts/cooldowns and passive. Once his E is on cooldown, he won't be able to space you. Look for patterns in how he combines his E with his Q casts. React to his E+Q combo by dashing into him with E and go for a short trade between his Q casts. Use W if you can't avoid the Q cast that follows. Punish him as much as possible whenever he uses his E throughout the laning phase.

Whenever Aatrox tries to combine his Q3 and E or tries to proc his Passive on you while his E is on cooldown, charge W into him and trade as long as his Q is on cooldown. If your E isn't on cooldown, continue the trade until his Q2/Q3 and disengage onto a minion. You can also E+W/Q on an allied minion if he walks up without E.
Stand behind minions and Aatrox won't be able to use W onto you to combo it with Qs. If he hits you with it, use your W to prevent the pull, run out, or use E towards a minion.

Look for all-ins between his Q casts/while his Q is on cooldown or once his E is on cooldown, even if he is in a healthy spot. Use All Out to stay on top of him and he won't be able to space you or hit his sweet spots, except for Q3. Hold E or W/RW for this. You can also use All Out to dodge his Q2 or Q3 hitbox. Charge RW during one of his Q casts while his E is on cooldown, and he won't be able to dodge it. His healing isn’t a major issue in the early game, even if he uses his R in return.

Managing your E becomes more important the lower Aatrox's Q cooldown gets. Eventually, his Q cooldown will be lower than your E, and his Q has a cooldown refund for every Q he doesn't cast after Q1. Make sure to track it.

If Aatrox goes Black Cleaver first, make sure that he can't keep the Black Cleaver stacks active on you with his Q poke. Just wait until the stacks run out before you engage. He isn't good at applying stacks quickly but can keep stacks up easily if you keep getting hit by his Q spam.

tldr: Space her Q's early. Use her forced E2 and R1 movements against her. Play safe until you get MR. Don't force fights with her W Shroud up/available.

Play around her W. Don't force trades once she uses it, or use Q3/W to push her out of it/stun her during the shroud duration. Make sure you know exactly where she is before using W, or she will turn on you and can punish you hard, using the Movement Speed it provides to hit you easily without being able to trade back effectively.

Once she hits you with E and uses the recast to dash to you, charge W into her. She is locked into the dash and can't avoid your W unless she uses Flash, but it isn't as easy to time if she is very close to you. You can do the same with her R1 and R2.

Her R1 forces her to dash behind you. React to her R1 cast by channeling W backward and release it as soon as possible. Most Akalis want to use their R1 end position to hit an almost guaranteed E, and stunning her with a well-timed W denies that setup (you can also sidestep/dodge with E). Her R2 requires more prediction than reaction. It is also a dash with a fixed distance rather than an end location. Depending on how close she is to you, its easy to figure out where she ends up once she uses it. (if shes closer she will dash further away, if shes far away then she will end up closer to you)

Her E2 and R2 deal a high amount of burst damage and Akali players like to combine them (E2 > R2 backwards once they are in your hitbox). If you still have W, make sure to use it for the Damage Reduction.
Be careful once you use All Out because it allows her to burst you a lot easier. Make sure to find an all-in window once her W/R are on cooldown or use RW to reduce the damage of her burst.
Once you initiate an all-in, she is able to use her R1 to buy a lot of time for her cooldowns before re-engaging.
She is very disruptive in fights because of her shroud and mobility, but all her dashes can be canceled if you time it well.
Pay attention to her position and ping your team if she tries to roam.

tldr: Survive early lane until Armor. Use E to block his Passive/Press the Attack. Cancel his E during trades/fights. Look for trades once his Passive Shield is on cooldown.

blocos.texto: The whole matchup revolves around denying her Vital procs. Vitals always rotate in 2 pairs: North and East or South and West. If she procs a North Vital, the next one will either be South or West.

You always want to position yourself in a way that makes it hard for her to hit Vitals. (If you have a North Vital, position above her; South Vital, below her; don’t walk up too close if the Vital is behind you). If the Vital is facing her, either trade it to last hit and block her proc with E or walk out of range to reset it. (Make sure you don't lose minion experience.)

Short trades mostly depend on how she uses her Q to hit a Vital. If you make it hard for her to proc it, she has to Q closer to you, allowing you to trade back with Q > AA, but if you allow her to proc it easily, she can hit it with a max range Q and you won't be able to trade back. You can also bait her to use her max range Q and move toward the opposite direction, causing her to miss you.

blocos.texto: Play safe early and let Wukong push the wave. He can deal a lot of damage early and his Passive grant's him a lot of Armor and sustain the longer you fight him.

Wukong want's to force extended trades onto you. If you are able to keep the wave near your tower, he won't be able to go for extended trades anymore or he is at risk of getting thrown into your tower.
Once the wave is near your tower, poke him with a short combo whenever he walks up for lasthits.
Kite back or use E whenever he walks up with Q or you expect him to Q you. It also reduces your Armor and affects your ability scalings.
When he tries to go for an extended fight, throw him under your tower, but make sure you don't waste everything on his W clone.
If his W is up when trying to all-in, use the clone against him. You can R it if he tries to escape with it or you R it to space out his R/R recast and chase him down after.
Use RW to block one of his R knock-ups.

tldr: Play safe until 6. Fight away from minions if possible.

blocos.texto: Avoid extended trades early (especially if he has Lethal Tempo) and play safe until level 6. Don't trade/fight inside the minion wave.
He will try to bully you early. Let him push and his movements with E will be very limited and he won't be able to force trades onto you.

Just stay back and dodge as many Q's as possible. If he hits no other target, he just wastes it, delay's getting a stack or the previous stacks run out. If he is close and tries to Q3 you, charge W into him, avoiding the knock-up and do a short trade while he is stunned. He can also E+Q to use Q as an aoe in a circle. Be mindful of your position and try to avoid it.
His Windwall only blocks your Q3. Be careful that he won't be able to re-engage by using E if you try to hit him with Q3 and over-commit.

Try to break his Passive shield's with Q whenever he dashes to you. Bramble Vest will eventually do that for you. Avoid trading while his Shield is up, but feel free to look for short trades whenever he comes to you and his Shield isn't up.
Look for All Out angles that isolate him from your minions and he has 0 mobility. Use W,R or RW to dodge his Q knock-up's.

Realistically, Yasuo shouldn't ever be allowed to knock you up on his own since his R provides him bonus armor pen on crits. This is especially dangerous while you are in All Out because of how Resistances are calculated (85% of your bonus resists is subtracted from your base resists. The more armor you get, the lower your base armor will be. Damage calculations with negative Armor behaves like a damage amp.)

Be careful if you have Aftershock. If he has his R passive active and you All Out him with the Aftershock effect proccing, he can kill you within a single Auto Attack. This is mainly because All Out recalculates your resistances in 0.25s intervals. If Aftershock runs out and the timing isn't aligned with one of those Server Ticks, you can end up in situations where Yasuo Auto's you at low double digit Armor values. Aftershock's resists also force your Base Armor during All Out to be even lower, essentially granting Yasuo even more damage amp.

tldr: Avoid extended fights. Charge W into him whenever he charges Q3 towards you.

blocos.texto: Avoid extended trades/fights early (especially if he has Lethal Tempo) and be careful of his powerspike at level 2/6.

Bait out his Q1/2 and/or sidestep them frequently. If he hits no other target, he just wastes it, delay's getting a stack or the previous stacks run out. If he is close and tries to Q3 you, charge W into him, avoiding the knock-up and do a short trade while he is stunned.

Look how aggressive Yone uses his W. If he uses it once he get's an oppertunity to hit you, bait it out by walking up to "fake lasthit" and kite back once he uses it. Trades are easier if he can't use it to shield himself.

Be careful once he uses E and play around his Bodies location. If you want to fight him, fight his Spirit close to his body to prevent him from using it as an escape once he decides to disengage. His E won't store damage done to shields, use E during it or at the very end for his recast damage.

If you all-in and he tries to escape with R, E>W into him, forcing him to stay next to you while soaking the knock-up and damage. This also allows you to hit a max charged RW. Make sure you aim your W into the direction he aims for since he will appear behind you.

If you fight close to his E and hold RW until his E almost expires, you can charge RW to hit a max charge the moment he is forced back into his body. You can also aim it in a path that will hit his body and Spirit.

Use All Out to cancel his Q3 dash. this requires a bit of timing and knowledge of yones q cd, you must cast it during his cast otherwise you won't pull him back. if you can cancel his retreat Q3  with your R he should be dead.
Be careful when fighting Lethal Tempo Yone. His Q cooldown, casttime and W cooldown rely on Attack Speed, which Lethal Tempo provides.

tldr: Dodge E's. Play around his W cage. Seperate him from his Maiden.

blocos.texto: Let Yorick push waves early and farm safely under tower.
Dodge his E at all cost and use your E to avoid it when necessary. If you get hit, you have to deal with his Ghouls, taking a lot of additional damage.
Use E to block his Q damage.
Be careful when trying to W him from some distance or he will place his W cage between you, blocking your W dash.
Make sure to get out of his cage when he casts it or use E onto an ally minion outside of it.
Look for trades once his W and/or E are on cooldown while managing your E cooldown/uses.
Use R to seperate him from his Maiden and you aren't stuck with the additional magic damage he gets from her. If he gets you locked in his W and walks up to auto you, use R to escape and turn on him.
Use RW if you are on top of him or while his W is on cooldown, otherwise he can block the dash with his W, locking you up. He can also barricade himself behind his W wall.
Yorick E reduces armor, dodge it by any means possible, do your best to avoid trading into his ghouls + maiden.

tldr: Play around his E and W cooldowns. Keep his health down with frequent short trades.

blocos.texto: Don’t be scared to fight Zaahen to the death early on after you’ve bought some armor. He lacks the cooldowns to keep fighting, and a fully stacked passive is not very scary early on. Worst case, you get his revive, which has a massive cooldown in the early game, allowing future plays, or you just kill him after the revive.
Try to maintain lane priority and/or minion advantage for level-up leads while forcing him to use abilities to CS.

Pay attention to when he uses Q1. He will use it frequently to heal on minions (unless you allow him to hit you). Wait until he uses his Q2 on minions or until it runs out before looking for a trade. Be careful if he tries to E > Q2 you and counter it with W.
Play more aggressively whenever he wastes his W early. It’s his main tool to chase you or stack his passive quickly.
Be careful when disengaging after a trade while his W is up, or he will be able to force an extended trade onto you.
Keep in mind that he can use his Q2 or W to cancel your W and E dash, potentially putting you in a bad spot if you aren’t careful.
Try to avoid the outer rim of his E as much as possible to avoid the additional damage.

Try to poke him down before going for an all-in if you want a clean kill without giving him time to proc his revive, or if you aren’t confident that you can proc his revive and still have time to kill him during R afterwards.

Try to bait his E or cancel it directly with R (It's less important if his R is on cooldown). One of those abilities alone isn’t enough to escape from you if you manage your E well, but both combined can be rough. Keep in mind that he can E/R over nearby walls.
Check his passive cooldown by clicking on him and looking at the buffs in the interface. If his revive isn’t up, look for aggressive plays.

Pay attention to his first item choice. If he goes Stridebreaker, he will lack damage against you and you can play more aggressively. Black Cleaver forces you to stick to short trades while he lacks waveclear. Trinity Force makes his short trades more dangerous, but his waveclear will still be weak. Poke him down as much as possible.
His R healing is bugged as of Patch 25.24. The healing is pre-mitigation, and using W/RW won’t change the amount he heals. (This line will be removed once fixed)

tldr: Deny as many blobs as possible to prevent his healing. Avoid getting hit by his Q or use W in response.

blocos.texto: Zac isn't stronger than you during the early lane. His entire gimmick is baiting you into extended fights while he tries to outheal your damage.
Look to freeze the wave near your tower, denying him the option to create blobs on minions, push to force plates or proxy.
During trades, focus on stepping onto his blobs. This prevent his healing and W cooldown refund. That way he will never win those trades.
Use your Q3 knock-up and Q3+W stun to buy you time to step on blobs.
Hold your W for his Q to block the displacement and stun. It also creates 2 blobs if you don't block it and gives him some time to collect his blobs. If you don't have W, sidestep it instead.
Sidestep or use W to block his E knock-up once he tries to engage for a gank.
All-in's are free if his E is on cooldown. You can also use R directly to cancel his E once he tries to charge it as an escape.
Once he uses R, use W/RW as an buffer through his cc.
Whenever he decides to E close to your tower, throw him in. You can stand in the hitbox and charge W to do so.
Zac want's to stack a lot of health and All Out just counters that.
His E is a good engage and he is very disruptive with his Q and R, but he needs to put points into E to get more range.
